summary:
TerraNexus is an interactive Earth-system trend investigation platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Be An Earth System Trend Detective. Users can choose a location on a 3D globe or search for a city, select an environmental variable and time range, and explore its historical time series.

Using NASA POWER data for supported meteorological variables, TerraNexus presents estimated rates of change per decade, confidence intervals, statistical significance, and data coverage. Its evidence-focused results explain the data sources, analysis assumptions, and scientific limitations, while sensitivity checks help users understand how results depend on the observations included.

TerraNexus makes complex Earth science data more accessible to students, researchers, and curious citizens by answering four essential questions: What is changing? Where is it changing? By how much? And how strong is the statistical evidence?
details:
What is TerraNexus?

TerraNexus is an interactive web application that helps users investigate long-term environmental changes using NASA Earth science data. It transforms complex environmental time series into accessible visualizations, statistical results, and understandable scientific explanations.

How Does It Work?

Users select an environmental variable, choose a location through an interactive 3D globe or worldwide city search, and specify a historical period.

For supported meteorological variables, TerraNexus uses NASA POWER data, including MERRA-2-derived records, to construct historical time series and investigate trends.

The application displays:

  • Historical environmental measurements and trend charts.
  • Estimated rates of change per decade.
  • Statistical significance and 95% confidence intervals.
  • Data coverage, missing observations, and uncertainty.
  • Scientific explanations and statistical diagnostic information.

The analysis uses linear regression on appropriately aggregated observations, with approximate Newey–West/HAC inference for temporal dependence where applicable.

What Makes TerraNexus Creative?

Our innovation is the combination of interactive Earth exploration with transparent scientific analysis.

The Evidence Trail helps users inspect original source values, statistical assumptions, data quality, and limitations instead of accepting results from a black box.

Sensitivity checks examine how estimated trends respond when individual years are excluded, helping users assess the stability of their conclusions.

Unlike a conventional weather dashboard, TerraNexus investigates historical environmental trends rather than forecasting future weather.

Benefits and Intended Impact

TerraNexus is designed for students, educators, researchers, and members of the public interested in environmental change. It makes NASA Earth science data easier to explore, understand, and critically evaluate.

Technology and Development

The project combines web development, interactive 3D geospatial visualization, NASA data services, and statistical analysis. The prototype uses Cesium-powered globe visualization and Open-Meteo/GeoNames-based location search.

OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT assisted with software development, debugging, research, planning, and presentation preparation. Scientific measurements are sourced from documented datasets, while numerical analyses are handled by application logic rather than generated as AI answers.

Limitations and Future Development

TerraNexus currently focuses on point-based estimates. NASA datasets have spatial resolution limitations, and statistical significance does not establish causation. Future improvements include expanding validated data coverage, strengthening statistical verification, and supporting additional NASA Earth observation products.
